title: Markdown extension: shorthand syntax that auto-links to an anchored target
description:
Writing a long document with a reference inventory means hand-writing the same
`[_Politics_](http://classics.mit.edu/Aristotle/politics.html)` link at every
mention. Want a shorthand that resolves to a declared target instead.

## Shape

Some special syntax at the call site, e.g. `{{politics}}` or `[[politics]]`, that
resolves to a target declared once — either an anchor elsewhere in the same
document, or a URL declared in a frontmatter/definition block. Exact syntax is
open; it must not collide with `[label](href)`, `[^footnote]`, or the existing
`{#id}` anchor marker.

## Prerequisite: `{#id}` anchors on list items

`split-trailing-anchor` (md.scm:267) already parses a trailing `{#id}` marker, but
it is only wired into headings (md.scm:89) and paragraphs (md.scm:288). List items
do not support it.

This matters because reference inventories are lists. In
`templates/bible/theology/monarchy/outline/index.md` the Part IX inventory is an
ordered list of ~150 works, and the only linkable targets are the seven `###`
subsection headings. Body citations therefore link to a whole subsection instead of
to the entry for the work being cited. Per-item anchors are what makes the
shorthand actually precise.

## Also worth deciding

Whether the shorthand's link text comes from the target (so the label is written
once) or is supplied at the call site, e.g. `[[politics|_Politics_ III.12]]`.
Citations frequently need a locator that the target does not carry.

## Motivation

The monarchy outline currently has ~86 hand-written citation links in its body.
Every one of them was applied mechanically and every one has to be maintained by
hand when a URL changes.

## Related

Follows the same "make prose into links without markdown syntax" goal as the
confession auto-linking bead, but it is generic rather than domain-specific.

title: Support footnotes in the markdown renderer
description:
The markdown renderer has no footnote support, so both halves of the syntax render
as literal text.

## Current behavior

`templates/bible/theology/monarchy/draft/index.md` uses seven footnotes. Rendering
it emits the raw markers verbatim — `[^1]` through `[^7]` each appear twice in the
output HTML (once at the call site, once in the Notes section) with no links and no
`<a>` tags at all.

## Scope

- Inline reference `[^label]` becomes a superscript link to the definition.
- Definition line `[^label]: text` is collected out of the body flow.
- Definitions render as an ordered list at the end of the document, each with a
  back-link to its call site.
- Definition bodies go through `parse-inline` (they contain emphasis and links —
  see the draft's Notes section).
- Labels are arbitrary strings, not just integers; number the rendered output by
  order of first reference rather than by label.
- Unreferenced definitions and undefined references should degrade to plain text
  rather than erroring.

## Implementation notes

- `parse-inline` (md.scm:143) is where the `[^label]` call site is recognized; it
  must be attempted before `parse-inline-link-at`, since both start with `[`.
- Collection is a document-level concern, so the definition pass belongs in
  `parse-markdown` / `md->html` rather than inline parsing.
- Generated ids must not collide with `text->id` heading anchors; prefix them
  (`fn-1`, `fnref-1`).
- Add a fixture pair under `scripts/lib/sxml/test/md/` and regenerate with
  `make test/regenerate`.

title: Support tables in the markdown renderer
description:
`parse-markdown` (`scripts/lib/md.scm:293`) handles headings, ordered/unordered
lists, fenced code, blockquotes and paragraphs. There is no table support, so
GitHub-flavored pipe tables render as literal text with visible `|` characters.

## Scope

Parse GFM pipe tables into `(table (thead ...) (tbody ...))` SXML:

```
| Author | Work | Date |
| ------ | ---- | ---- |
| Aristotle | _Politics_ | c. 350 BCE |
```

- Header row, delimiter row, body rows.
- Honor the delimiter row's alignment colons (`:--`, `:-:`, `--:`) as `style="text-align:..."`
  or an alignment class.
- Cell contents go through `parse-inline`, so emphasis and links work inside cells.
- Ragged rows: pad or truncate to the header's column count rather than erroring.

## Notes

- `markdownlint` config already sets MD013 `line_length: 120`; wide tables will
  trip it, so check whether MD013's `tables: false` option should be set in
  `.markdownlint.yaml`.
- The theme stylesheet (`/shared/styles/openword-theme.css`) has no table styling
  yet — needs at least borders and cell padding, and horizontal scroll on narrow
  viewports.
- Add a fixture pair under `scripts/lib/sxml/test/md/` and regenerate with
  `make test/regenerate`.

## Motivation

The monarchy research references are CSVs served as raw asset downloads
(`assets/bible/theology/monarchy/research/references/*.csv`). With table support
they could render as readable on-page tables instead.

title: Auto-link confession notations the way scripture references are linked
description:
`scripts/lib/md.scm` already turns bare scripture references in prose into links:
`linkify-scripture` (md.scm:533-577) walks the parsed SXML, matches book names via
`match-book-at`, and emits anchors against `%scripture-base-url` using
`chapter-anchor` / `verse-anchor`. Pages opt out with `scripture-links: false` in
frontmatter.

Do the same for confessional citations, so writing `1689 ch. 23` or `WCF 22.3` in
prose produces a link with no markdown syntax.

## Forms to recognize

- Second London Baptist Confession: `1689 ch. 23`, `LBCF 23`, `LBCF 23.4`, `2LBCF 24.1`
- Westminster Confession: `WCF 22`, `WCF 23.3`, `Westminster Confession ch. 22`
- Catechisms: Baptist Catechism (1695) and Heidelberg by question number (`HC Q.101`)

Chapter-only and chapter.paragraph should both work, matching how the scripture
linker handles chapter vs. verse.

## Prerequisite

There is nothing in the repo to link *to* — the reference CSVs under
`assets/bible/theology/monarchy/research/references/` contain no confessional
documents. This needs a decision first:

1. Host the confession texts as site content (mirrors the Bible versions approach,
   gives stable in-site anchors, most work), or
2. Link out to canonical public texts (fast, but no anchors per paragraph).

Option 1 is what makes the scripture linker work well and is probably the right
target.

## Reuse notes

`linkify-scripture-node` deliberately skips URLs, existing links, code spans, raw
passthrough, and headings (md.scm:558-573) — a confession linker must respect the
same exclusions, so factor that traversal rather than duplicating it.

## Motivation

`templates/bible/theology/monarchy/outline/index.md` cites the 1689 and Westminster
about 25 times in prose. Those are currently hand-linked to a section anchor, which
is a workaround, not a destination.
